# VP9 header fixture

`header.ivf` contains three 32×32 synthetic testsrc2 frames, generated locally:

```sh
ffmpeg -v error -f lavfi -i 'testsrc2=size=32x32:rate=3:duration=1' \
  -an -c:v libvpx-vp9 -threads 1 -lag-in-frames 0 -g 30 \
  -f ivf header.ivf
```

This fixture contains no user media. FFmpeg/libvpx are fixture-generation and
independent inspection tools, not runtime dependencies of the native decoder.
`ffmpeg -i header.ivf -c:v copy -bsf:v trace_headers -f null -` independently
reports key/inter/inter, quantizer indices 37/128/119, loop filter levels 0/4/8,
and compressed-header lengths 34/3/3 bytes. Native tests verify these fields,
reference size inheritance, show-existing handling, truncation atomicity, and
arithmetic-coded keyframe header parsing. Picture reconstruction is covered by the pixel oracles below.

## Picture and transform oracles

`header-first.yuv` and `header-all.yuv` are raw yuv420p decodes of `header.ivf`.
`transforms.bin` is generated by `scripts/vp9_transform_oracle.c`, linked only in
that external test generator to libvpx. It contains 448 deterministic 8-bit pixel
blocks covering all valid DCT/ADST/WHT sizes and combinations.

Additional synthetic WebM sequences use `testsrc2`, libvpx-vp9, `-threads 1
-lag-in-frames 0 -auto-alt-ref 0 -frame-parallel 1`:

- `motion.webm`: `size=128x96:rate=10:duration=1`, `-g 4 -crf 33 -b:v 0`.
- `odd10.webm`: `size=70x50:rate=3:duration=1`, `-pix_fmt yuv420p10le -g 2
  -crf 30 -b:v 0`.
- `lossless12.webm`: `size=48x32:rate=3:duration=1`, `-pix_fmt yuv420p12le
  -g 2 -lossless 1`.

Each matching `.yuv` is generated with `ffmpeg -i FILE.webm -fps_mode passthrough
-pix_fmt FORMAT -f rawvideo FILE.yuv`, using the corresponding 8/10/12-bit 4:2:0
format. Tests compare every decoded sample; high-bit-depth files are little-endian.
